title: A failed fetch is not cached as a permanent absence
question_or_target: Is a transient fetch failure negatively cached with a SHORT ttl and clearly distinguished from a genuine absence? PASS requires a retry after the negative-ttl to hit the network again; an empty result that reports OK is the failure being tested.

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer verified the artifact at command-center/receipts/TST-0176.json exists on disk (24882 LF-normalized bytes), parses as JSON, carried the builder terminal state=BLOCKED with failure.classification=[reviewer-absent] and reviewer=null (no self-certification) at review time, and its report.kind=cache_report matches the catalog output_schema pin.

probes.raw_output: parsed OK; builder state=BLOCKED; classification=[reviewer-absent]; reviewer=null

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer re-ran both named probes live for 3 rounds each under the ambient environment; all exited 0 with the unit SUCCESS sentinel (probe1_negative_ttl.py=3/3 rounds rc0; probe2_genuine_404.py=3/3 rounds rc0); live sentinels match the builder-recorded raw_output lines (consistent=True).
